title: The Friend has come home
hook: the Friend has come to my home; the True One brought us together (Suhi M1, ang 764)

segments.voice: Yesterday, sir, the head under the Master's hand, and your line: guarded. Today, a hymn of arrival, sung at Sikh weddings.

The doorbell rings and you already know who it is. A brother back from deployment, a daughter home from her first semester, an old friend you haven't seen in ten years. You open the door and the whole house changes. Somebody starts cooking. Guru Nanak wrote a hymn for exactly that instant, when the one you've waited for crosses the threshold. And it is sung on a wedding morning.
screen: `THE DOORBELL RINGS.` → `THE WHOLE HOUSE CHANGES.` → `A HYMN FOR THE THRESHOLD.`

segments.voice: The hymn is a chhant, a longer song form, in Raag Suhi, on ang 764. It opens, in effect: the friend has come to my home; the True One has brought about this meeting. The meeting came naturally, pleasing to the Lord's mind; I've found what my heart was set on. Night and day there is union, my mind is content, my home and temple are made beautiful. The unstruck music plays. The word is saajan: friend, beloved, the dear one. The verb, aae, can be read as one honored friend or many, and the hymn holds both. On the surface, guests arriving for a celebration. Underneath, the Beloved, the One, arriving in the heart. Tradition links Raag Suhi with weddings, and this chhant is sung at Sikh weddings before the couple walks the lavan. You can see why. A family's home fills with friends. Two people are brought together, and the hymn says plainly who did it: the True One made the meeting. And beneath it all, Gurbani's image of the soul as a bride waiting for the Beloved to come home. Notice the order: the arrival first, then the house becomes beautiful. The home doesn't have to be perfect before the friend comes. The coming makes it beautiful. Tomorrow, the first of the four wedding rounds.
screen: `SAAJAN: FRIEND, BELOVED.` · `THE TRUE ONE MADE THE MEETING.` · `SUNG AS A WEDDING BEGINS.` · `THE COMING MAKES THE HOUSE BEAUTIFUL.` · then, large: `THE FRIEND IS HOME.`

segments.voice: Picture your own front door, and someone you love walking through it, someone coming soon or someone you wish would; see their face as the door opens, and let whatever gladness comes be as big as it wants. If you pray, welcome the One the same way, with a quiet Waheguru, as if the One were the friend at the door; if not, simply rest in the welcome.
Saajan, friend, beloved, the dear one: Guru Nanak's wedding chhant says the saajan has come to my home, the True One made the meeting, and the house is made beautiful.
Your line: the friend is home. The house doesn't have to be ready first. Day six hundred sixty-one, done.

howItsDone: Sikhs sing Guru Nanak's Suhi chhant 'ham ghar saajan aae' in kirtan, and it is sung at the Anand Karaj, the wedding, before the lavan.

trapdoor: what you thought: a song about guests arriving.
what it means: guests and the Beloved at once: the True One makes the meeting and the house becomes beautiful.
what a scholar hears: the Suhi chhant uses bridal imagery for the soul's union with the One; anahad shabad, the unstruck music, marks it as mystical union as well as celebration.

chat.says: There's a Sikh wedding hymn about a friend coming home. Who's the friend?
options: The guests, and the One arriving in the heart; the True One made the meeting.
Only a traveler the family took in for one night on his journey.
Only the guests; it's just a welcome song with no deeper meaning.
chat.meaning: In Guru Nanak's Suhi chhant, saajan can be friends arriving and the Beloved arriving in the heart; the True One brings the meeting about.
